_comment: The travel map of central Gaul. One cell is roughly 12 km. Rows are drawn north (top) to south. Rules: src/core/world_data.gd.

locations.name: Brigodunon
locations.desc: Home. A hill fort of the Cadurci above the Oltis, behind a rampart of stone and timber.

locations.name: The Grotto of the Hanging Dead
locations.desc: A cave in the limestone where the old dead were hung for the birds. Nobody goes there now. Somebody does.

locations.name: Vindomagos
locations.desc: A farming village on the north bank of the Oltis. Salt, grain, and gossip.

locations.name: The ford at the Oltis
locations.desc: The only good crossing of the Oltis for a day in either direction.

locations.name: Uxellodunum
locations.desc: The great stronghold of the Cadurci, on its cliff above the Duranius.
locations.closed_text: The road goes on, but this part of Gaul isn't built yet. The way home is open.

locations.name: Gergovia
locations.desc: The Arverni capital on its plateau. Whoever holds it holds the revolt.
locations.shut_text: The gates are shut. Gobannitio's men hold the plateau, and the valley below it is full of his nephew's ragged army. Nobody gets in, and anyone who tries to get out is looked at very closely. Come back when one of them has won.

locations.name: Avaricum
locations.desc: The richest city in Gaul, behind walls of stone and timber.

locations.name: Noviodunum
locations.desc: Caesar's depot on the Liger, in the country of the Aedui. Hostages, horses, grain, and the army's pay.

closed_by_flag.text: Noviodunum is ash. The Aedui have gone over to the revolt, and their young men came over the stakes at night, killed every Roman in the depot, and took the horses, the money and the grain. The hostages of every people in Gaul went east to Bibracte, in Aeduan carts, to be bargained with.

locations.name: Cenabum
locations.desc: The Carnute trading town on the Liger where the revolt began.

locations.name: The Carnute forest
locations.desc: Where the druids of all Gaul meet once a year.
locations.closed_text: The road goes on, but this part of Gaul isn't built yet. The way home is open.

locations.name: Bibracte
locations.desc: The Aeduan capital. Rome's oldest friends in Gaul.
locations.closed_text: The road goes on, but this part of Gaul isn't built yet. The way home is open.

locations.name: Alesia
locations.desc: A hill town of the Mandubii.
locations.closed_text: The road goes on, but this part of Gaul isn't built yet. The way home is open.

encounters.text: A lone wolf, ribs showing, has been following your tracks.
Wolves. Winter has made them bold.
Two wolves are shadowing you through the brush.
A man with an axe and a hungry look steps out of the brush. He's alone, or wants you to think so.

parley.label: Pay him
parley.text: You hold out the coins. He counts them, spits, and steps aside. 'Safe road,' he says, and means the opposite.

parley.label: Talk
parley.win: You talk about the war, the cold and the next village, and the longer you talk the less he wants an argument. He lets you by.
parley.lose: He listens to the end and then hits you with the flat of the axe. Talking is over.

encounters.text: Two men on the road with weapons and no village. In a war, that's a trade.

parley.label: Pay them
parley.text: You pay. The slinger takes the coins and the axeman takes his time, but they let you by.

parley.label: Talk
parley.win: You tell them what the Romans do to men like them, and what Brigodunon does to men who rob its people. They look at each other and let you pass.
parley.lose: They're not in a listening mood. The axeman starts toward you.

encounters.text: A gang on the road with weapons and no village. In a war, that's a trade.

parley.label: Pay them
parley.text: It costs you, and the leader makes a show of counting it, but they step off the road.

parley.label: Talk
parley.win: Three men and no good answer for why you would be worth the trouble. The leader waves you on, and you walk away slowly.
parley.lose: The leader smiles. The other two spread out.

parley.label: Slip away
parley.win: You back into the trees without turning your back on them, and keep going until the road is only a sound.
parley.lose: A branch cracks under your foot. All three heads turn.

encounters.text: A family on the road, carrying everything they own.
A trader with two mules, a guard, and opinions.
A Roman soldier and an auxiliary slinger, a long way from their camp, stripping a farm. They see you.

parley.label: Pay him off
parley.text: The soldier weighs the silver, and what it's worth against a report. He has never seen you.

parley.label: Speak Latin
parley.win: You greet them in their own tongue and give a name that could be anyone's. The soldier waves you on as one more native who keeps out of the way.
parley.lose: Your Latin runs out in the middle of a sentence. The soldier draws his gladius.

parley.label: Slip away
parley.win: You go to ground in a ditch and wait them out. They never look your way.
parley.lose: A dog barks at you from the farmyard. The soldier turns.

encounters.text: Roman foragers, a long way from their camp, stripping a farm. They see you.

parley.label: Pay them off
parley.text: It takes everything that can be spared, but they take it. None of them looks at you again.

parley.label: Speak Latin
parley.win: You speak slowly and politely, like a man with nothing to hide, and they lose interest.
parley.lose: They don't believe a word. The sergeant calls an order.

parley.label: Slip away
parley.win: You stay low behind the wall until they've finished and gone. You don't breathe much.
parley.lose: One of them sees the movement and shouts. They come over the wall.
